feedback: The confession follows my strongest pre-vote inference: the claimed private permission was false, and the person admitting poison handling had the most directly relevant lie. It feels emotionally earned when Dada abandons an artistic explanation and asks Vincent not to supply one. Elle and Monet's aftermaths also keep their separate wrongdoing alive rather than resetting them to innocent bystanders. The confession does newly establish Dada's private-room entry and deliberate glass contamination after his categorical denial; I had no independent observation of that encounter. That is a remaining evidential limitation, although the rejected live stunt gave a fair route to suspecting the denial was false.
new_decisive_facts: Dada newly admits entering the private room and contaminating the unattended glass, reversing his earlier denial without an independently supplied placement at that glass.
